items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: I didn’t like making personnel changes, because we had rehearsed these pieces scrupulously. I didn’t want new guys coming in and having to learn that. When a new

trumpet player came into my band, the first few nights, or week or two, his upper lip would be . . . his embouchure would be terrible. It would swell up, because I had him bending notes that trumpet players didn’t do much. And I had him doing things that would . . . the saxes and brass blended. When they played an ensemble . . . it was I think the best ensemble band that ever lived. I don’t think anybody ever [had a] better ensemble band. What’s his name? Jimmie Lunceford sometimes came close. But I think…
I always liked the 1939 recording of I Surrender, Dear for the sax section. It is extraordinary.
